name: Alexandria Real Estate Equities
description: Alexandria owns and develops laboratory and office campuses for life-science companies, mainly in Greater Boston, the San Francisco Bay Area, San Diego, Seattle, Maryland, Research Triangle, New York City and Texas. Tenants, many of them pharmaceutical and biotech companies, sign long leases, with about 97 percent of leases (by annual rental revenue) carrying escalations of roughly 3 percent a year and 53 percent of annual rental revenue coming from investment-grade or publicly traded large-cap tenants. The company also builds new space, spending $1.44 billion on construction in 2025. In FY2025 it reported a net loss attributable to common stockholders of about $1.4 billion after real estate and other impairments, and on December 3, 2025 it cut its quarterly dividend 45 percent from $1.32 to $0.72 per share. It is selling properties and, in Q2 2026, again recorded a large impairment ($222.5 million).

gics.note: Conventional label recorded from general knowledge of the standard scheme; not re-checked against an MSCI/S&P source in this pass. SEC SIC code is 6798 (Real Estate Investment Trusts). The box misleads: these are laboratory and life-science campuses in a handful of clusters (Boston, San Francisco Bay, San Diego), leased mostly to pharma, biotech and large-cap tenants, so demand follows biotech funding and drug-development activity rather than office employment. Its tenants and its exposure to FDA workforce cuts, tariffs and venture funding are closer to a biotech-infrastructure landlord.
